title: Policy exemption transitive fanout causing unmetered requests
creator: Ethan Park
description: Summary: We observed a class of requests that bypass metering when a per-route exemption includes an alias/wildcard and the request fanouts to multiple internal sub-routes. The policy evaluator memoizes exemption results keyed insufficiently, causing exemptions to be applied transitively to child routes. This results in missing meter events and underbilling for affected orgs during fanout-heavy workloads.
observed_behavior: Large-scale batch requests that expand into N sub-requests (fanout) sometimes generate zero meter events for the child routes when the parent route is marked as exempt for certain orgs/keys. We saw this on prod region-us-east-1 between 2026-02-28T23:00 and 2026-03-01T03:00 with a spike in unaccounted tokens and a coincident billing gap reported by finance.
expected_behavior: Exemptions should be scoped to the explicit route policy where configured. A parent route exemption must not implicitly mark independent child/sub-route meters as exempt unless those routes explicitly include the exemption rule. Meter events should be emitted for every executed sub-route unless the sub-route policy explicitly exempts them.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create org 'acme-test' and add API key with per-key allowance
2) Configure route '/jobs' with an exemption for 'acme-test' that uses an alias pattern '/jobs/*'
3) Configure child routes '/jobs/emit' and '/jobs/worker' with default (non-exempt) policy
4) Send a single request that fanouts: POST /jobs -> internally calls /jobs/emit and /jobs/worker
5) Observe metrics: the parent request shows as exempt and neither child route emitted meter events in the policy agent logs; billing pipeline shows missing tokens for those executions.
root_cause_analysis: The policy evaluator maintains a small LRU memoization cache keyed by route ID only. When evaluating an exemption that uses a wildcard/alias, the memoized entry is reused across evaluations for the same actor/org pair without including the evaluated request's target route identifier and policy origin. In fanout scenarios the memoized 'exempt=true' result is applied to sub-route evaluations even though the exemption was intended for the parent route only. Race conditions in the policy cache warm path make the behavior more likely under bursty fanout.
proposed_fix: 1) Extend the policy memoization key to include the policy origin and the concrete target route identifier so exemptions are not applied transitively. 2) Add a strict scoping check in the evaluator: wildcard exemptions should only match when the route canonical path resolution verifies origin match. 3) Add a config flag 'policy.experimental.strict_exemption_scoping' default true to gate behavior during rollout.
code_changes: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4521 - evaluator: include policy_origin & target_route in cache key
PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4523 - add strict scoping logic and feature gate
PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1189 - add canary job and smoke test for meter emission
tests: Unit: policy_evaluator_cache_key_tests (new) - verify cache key includes origin+target
Integration: fanout_metering_integration (new) - orchestrates a parent route + 2 child routes and asserts meter events for children
E2E: billing-reconciliation-smoke (updated) - synthetic workload ensuring no missing tokens
rollout_plan: 1) Merge PRs to main and run full CI (unit + integration)
2) Deploy to staging (canary group) and run fanout integration job for 24h
3) Deploy to one production canary cluster (region: us-east-1) with feature gate enabled for 10% of traffic
4) Monitor billing reconciliation and meter event ratios for 48h; if green, ramp to 50% then 100% over 24h
5) Backfill missing meter events where possible via reconciliation job (see mitigation)
monitoring_and_mitigation: Create alert 'billing.missing_meter_rate > 0.5% over 1h' tied to runbook ENG-203744-RUNBOOK
Temporary mitigation: disable wildcard alias exemptions for high-volume routes via admin UI (manual config)
Reconciliation: run offline event-join job to estimate missing tokens and generate corrective invoices / credits
Dashboard: add 'fanout-metering-coverage' panel to console runtime dashboards (linked below)
notes: Finance queued a customer inquiry for March 2nd about unexplained billing deltas; we should coordinate public-facing comms if reconciliation shows user-facing impact.
Design: no UI changes required except temporary admin toggle for exemptions; product agreed to add longer-term guardrails in console UX.
Security: no direct data leakage risk identified; policy behavior change only affects billing logic (security_review_required=false).
Follow-ups: add a fuzz test for complex alias trees (ENG-203745 planned) and audit other memoization caches in the rate engine.
